arc-agi.description: Infer a new transformation rule from example grids; reproduce the target grid without a written instruction.
arc-agi.input: Example input/output grid pairs and a test grid
arc-agi.assessment: Grid dimensions and all cell values must match
arc-agi.date_note: Original paper v1; ARC-AGI-1 is the later official name for this edition.

math.description: Solve contest math problems with exact final answers; the dataset also provides worked solutions.
math.output: Final mathematical answer, optionally with working
math.assessment: Normalized final answer compared with the reference

gsm8k.description: Translate a word problem into several arithmetic steps and return a numerical answer.
gsm8k.output: Numerical final answer, optionally with working
gsm8k.assessment: Final number matched against the reference answer

big-bench-hard.description: Test reasoning on a deliberately difficult subset of 23 existing BIG-bench tasks.
big-bench-hard.input: Task prompt with choices or short-answer format
big-bench-hard.assessment: Accuracy against reference answers across 23 tasks

gpqa.description: Answer expert-written multiple-choice science questions designed to challenge knowledgeable nonexperts.
gpqa.input: Expert-written science question and four options

olympiadbench.description: Solve bilingual competition problems, distinguishing automatically scored final answers from proof problems.
olympiadbench.input: Olympiad problem, sometimes with a diagram
olympiadbench.output: Mathematical or physical answer; some problems request proof
olympiadbench.assessment: Reported automatic accuracy covers non-proof final answers
olympiadbench.first_author_affil: Dept. of Comp. Sci. & Tech., Institute for AI, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China

frontiermath.description: Solve original expert-written math problems with answers that can be verified automatically.
frontiermath.output: Numerical answer or specified mathematical object
frontiermath.assessment: Verification script checks the answer or its properties

arc-agi-2.description: Infer a transformation rule from example grid pairs and apply it to a new grid.
arc-agi-2.input: Example input/output grid pairs and a test input
arc-agi-2.assessment: Dimensions and every cell must match the target

arc-agi-3.description: Explore an unfamiliar game, infer its goals and advance through levels. A solver can write code, but the benchmark grades its actions, not its source code.
arc-agi-3.input: Observations from an unfamiliar interactive environment
arc-agi-3.output: Actions that reach the level goals
arc-agi-3.assessment: Relative Human Action Efficiency (RHAE), using human action baselines
arc-agi-3.date_note: Official full benchmark launch on March 25. The technical report was submitted March 24; the preview was released July 17, 2025.

alternative_dates.note: arXiv v1 submission, not the full launch event.

gamebench.description: Play board games, card games and social-deduction games against other agents. GameBench scores strategic play; it does not ask the model to build a game.
gamebench.input: Game rules and the current state; most are text, Hive can use an image
gamebench.output: A move or action for the current turn
gamebench.assessment: Aggregate pairwise game outcomes with a Bradley–Terry rating model.
gamebench.date_note: First public paper; most games use text states, while Hive also supports image observations.

arc-agi-3-preview.description: Explore an early set of interactive games and infer their rules. This developer preview and its competition are distinct from the full 2026 benchmark.
arc-agi-3-preview.input: Grid observations from the preview games
arc-agi-3-preview.output: A sequence of legal game actions
arc-agi-3-preview.assessment: The preview competition ranked performance on held-back games by levels completed, with tie-breaks; not the full 2026 RHAE score.
arc-agi-3-preview.date_note: Retrospective from the maintainer explicitly dates the public preview to July 17. The competition kickoff was July 18.

reasoning-arena.description: Answer a suite of math, logic and multistep questions.
reasoning-arena.assessment: Question-specific grading with score, time and cost reporting; distinct from the same-name trace-tournament training paper.

mm-arena.description: Quote prices in an explicitly specified market-making game. MM means market making here.
mm-arena.input: A market description and trade observations.
mm-arena.assessment: Expected trading performance relative to a Bayesian reference quoter.

game-arena.description: Play, not build: in Kaggle Game Arena, models face one another in chess, poker and Werewolf. Their match results determine the standings within each game.
game-arena.input: Game rules and the observed state or history in the published text protocols
game-arena.output: A legal move, bet or dialogue action, depending on the game
game-arena.assessment: Compare models by head-to-head game outcomes under each game’s scoring protocol.
